items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: I had to wind up, with the exception of my banjo player who was Talcott Reeves.

ctx.x: Right. Fine. Then, did you -- when you took the band to New York from Wilberforce, did most all of the players that had been working with you go and stay with you or did some of them stay back in school, or what was the situation with that?

Well, no. Some of these fellas didn't make music their career, and I had to wind up, with the exception of my banjo player who was Talcott Reeves. He's in New York now, and he's the Vice President of a Butcher's Association there. He doesn't play any more. But that little guy was great though. He was one of the originals, from Fort Smith, Arkansas. Talcott Reeves. He was (inaudible). went to school with me. We went to New York. The McCord brothers, Theodore and Castor, went to New York. And these are some of the…
Okay. Were the arrangements that you were using at that time, were they still a lot of them ones that Fletcher had given you, or were you writing your own?
